headline: Adopted release of Lowell Housing Authority land restrictions; referred several requests, including Woburn Street safety plan and school bus cameras, to City Manager.
summary: Members adopted the release of land restrictions for Lowell Housing Authority property by a roll call vote of 10 yeas. Several requests on street safety, school bus cameras, traffic, permits, and fire calls were referred to the City Manager. Motion responses, reports, resignations, and a claim were accepted, placed on file, or referred.
decisions: Accepted and placed on file a communication on remote Zoom participation.
Accepted and placed on file the minutes of the October 6 Rules & Election Law SC meeting and the October 6 City Council Regular Meeting.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a real-time system to search building permits as they are issued.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a plan to improve safety along Woburn Street, including evaluating a ban on on-street parking at 178–194 Woburn Street.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a report on the newly installed mini forest and pollinator garden in Centralville.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a report on a path forward for a pilot camera program on school buses that transport Lowell students.
Referred to the City Manager a request for plans on which streets and sidewalks will be paved, repaired, or traffic calmed in 2027.
Referred to the City Manager a request for information on the benefits and costs of firefighters and fire trucks responding to non-fire calls, and on alternatives.
Referred to the City Manager a request for traffic monitoring on Beacon Street and for clearer signage or a trained crossing guard at school dismissal times.
Accepted and placed on file the motion response on the vacancy ordinance.
Accepted and placed on file the motion response on short term rentals.
Accepted and placed on file the motion response on the reservoir.
Accepted and placed on file the motion response on the portrait of Mayor Palmer.
Accepted and placed on file the motion response on social districts.
Referred the social districts matter to the Economic Development SC.
Accepted and placed on file the resignations of James Harmon, Nayeli Pimentel, Judith Huber, and Kevin Dillon from city boards and commissions.
Adopted on second reading the release of land restrictions for the Lowell Housing Authority, by roll call vote of 10 yeas.
Accepted the Rules & Election Law SC report of October 6, 2026, as a report of progress.
Accepted the Housing SC report of October 13, 2026, as a report of progress.
Referred a property damage claim to the Law Department for a report and recommendation.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
Date:        October 13, 2026
Time:        6:30 PM
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, 
Lowell, MA / Zoom (Hybrid)
1. ROLL CALL
Roll Call showed 10 present (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. 
Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. 
Scott).
M. Gitschier presiding.
2. MAYOR'S BUSINESS
2.1. Communication Remote / Zoom Participation.
In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Robinson, 
seconded by C. Scott.  So voted.
Motion to suspend rules to allow Peg Shanahan to speak about Lowell and 
the UNESCO Learning City Program.  So voted.  Ms. Shanahan noted the 
recent award received by the City and the many upcoming events regarding 
the program.  M. Gitschier noted that October was Learning City Month for 
the City.
Motion by C. Chau, seconded by C. Descoteaux to take Item #6.1 out of 
order.  So voted.  
3. CITY CLERK
3.1. Minutes of Rules & Election Law SC October 6th; City Council 
Regular Meeting October 6th, for acceptance.
Office of the City Clerk
City Hall • 375 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852
P: 978.674.4161 • F: 978.970.4162
www.LowellMA.gov

City Clerk

In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. McDonough, 
seconded by C. Liang.  So voted.
4. CITY COUNCIL - MOTIONS
4.1. C. Scott - Req. City Mgr. work with the appropriate department to 
develop and implement a system that provides the public with real-
time access to search for building permits as they are issued. 
In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  C. Scott noted the request of residents and that it would be a simple 
task with little costs.  C. McDonough noted difficulty with permit violations 
complaints done during the weekends.  C. Nuon noted that notice is 
provided to some during the permitting process.
4.2. C. Scott - Req. City Mgr. work with the Traffic Engineer to develop
a plan to improve safety along Woburn Street, including evaluating 
the prohibition of on-street vehicle parking along 178–194 Woburn 
Street to improve sight lines and visibility for pedestrians and 
motorists.
In City Council, seconded by C. Juran, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
C. Scott noted resident concerns with safety because of street 
infrastructure.  Manager Golden, Jr. made note of the area and where the 
issues were present.
4.3. C. Robinson - Req. City Mgr. have the proper department provide 
a report on the newly installed mini forest as well as the pollinator 
garden in Centralville.
In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  Motion by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Mercier to take Item 
#5.1(C) up for discussion here.  So voted.  C. Robinson requested the plan 
for future work for plantings and at the reservoir.  
4.4. C. Robinson / C. Descoteaux - Req. City Mgr. have the proper 
department provide a report providing a path forward to implement a

pilot camera program on a selection of school buses assigned to 
transporting Lowell students.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  So voted.  C. 
Descoteaux noted the upcoming budget and the need to plan for this 
expense and that a pilot program would be more cost effective.  C. 
Robinson noted this is about safety and that if it is a pilot program would it 
need the support of the School Committee.  C. Descoteaux noted the next 
step is to get before the School Committee.
4.5. C. Juran - Req. City Mgr. have DPW and Transportation Engineer 
prepare, by early 2027 or as appropriate, plans for which streets and 
sidewalks will be paved, otherwise repaired, or traffic calmed in 2027 
and how consistent the prioritization is with the decision flow-charts.
In City Council, seconded by C. Liang, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
C. Juran noted residents are anxious about street paving and traffic flow 
moving forward and further noted that 2026 information is used for 2027 
schedules.  C. Nuon noted the need for a flow chart every year as 2026 
work could enter 2027 schedules.  C. Robinson noted there could be 
changes in ratings from year to year for streets due to outside factors.  
Manager Golden, Jr. noted information changes and that there are updates 
to the charts.  C. Juran noted that there are changes but the criteria must 
remain consistent.  
4.6. C. Juran - Req. City Mgr. have proper departments explain 
benefits and costs of having firefighters and fire trucks respond to 
non-fire calls (including EMS and helipad calls) and the costs and 
feasibility of alternatives.
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
C. Juran noted the need to support safety departments but there must be 
an understanding on how resources are used.  C. Nuon noted concerns 
with costs in safety departments and that a balanced approach must be 
used.  C. Robinson noted the need to protect the equipment from overuse.  
C. Mercier noted the need to have fire department on all calls as there is a

need for response from someone.  C. McDonough noted costs could be 
transferred to communities that benefit from the services.  C. Liang 
questioned type of calls outside of fire calls.  Manager Golden, Jr. outlined 
the various calls to the department.  C. Juran noted the need to look 
towards efficiency.  C. Nuon noted report could go to a subcommittee.    
4.7. M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. Have The Traffic Engineer Monitor 
The Traffic Being Held Back On Beacon Street From 9:05 To 9:30am 
And Again At The Robinson School Dismissal Between 2:05 And 
2:25pm; There Is Also A Need For Clearer Signage Or A Trained 
Crossing Guard During These Heavy Traffic Times. 
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
5. COMMUNICATIONS FROM CITY MANAGER
5.1. Motion Responses.
A) Motion Response - Vacancy Ordinance - In City Council, Motion “To 
accept and place on file” by C. Liang, seconded by C. Juran.  So voted.  C. 
McDonough made note of the Inn and Conference Center for UML, 
indicating the condition of the property in the back.  C. Robinson 
commented on properties near the Church Street area indicating the 
condition and the vacancy for some time.  Manager Golden, Jr. Noted they 
have been fined and the issue is that it is a legacy property with some 
internal strife.  C. Robinson noted there may be a need to adjust penalties 
under the ordinance.  City Solicitor Williams noted there can be changes 
made if it complies with statute.  C. Nuon noted report section regarding the
Inn and Conference Center and questioned plans for the site.  Manager 
Golden, Jr. indicated the conservations with parties regarding the site and 
that the City is at the table for them.  C. McDonough noted the need for 
fines as the vacancy of the building is affecting the whole area.  
B) Motion Response - Short Term Rentals - In City Council, Motion “To 
accept and place on file” by C. Chau, seconded by C. Juran.  So voted.  
Registered speaker, Mordecai Ese Ebhohon (comment – explore some 
steps that could be done to allow short term rentals as there is a tourist 
benefit for it), addressed the Council.  C. Juran noted the need to see the

regulations and rules for short term rentals and boarding houses.  C. Chau 
noted that there are a number in the City.  Yovani Baez-Rose (DPD) noted 
the need to educate owners and to warn those who are violating.
C) Motion Response – Reservoir - In City Council, Motion “To accept and
place on file” by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Nuon.  So voted.  See 
discussion under Item #4.3.  
D) Motion Response - Portrait Mayor Palmer - In City Council, Motion 
“To accept and place on file” by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Mercier.  So 
voted.  M. Gitschier thanked the Historic Board.
E) Motion Response - Social Districts - In City Council, Motion “To 
accept and place on file” by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Scott.  So voted.
Motion to refer matter to Economic Development SC by C. Robinson, 
seconded by C. Scott.  So voted.  C. Mercier did not support having open 
containers downtown.  
5.2. Communication - Resignations of Members from Various Boards 
and Commissions. In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” 
by C. Liang, seconded by C. Descoteaux.  So voted.  The following 
resignations were accepted: James Harmon (Veterans Commission); 
Nayeli Pimentel (Veterans Commission); Judith Huber (Council on Aging) 
and Kevin Dillon (Conservation Commission).  C. Robinson noted that there
are more resignations appearing before the body.  Manager Golden, Jr. 
noted they are moving on attempting to fill vacancies.
5.3. Communication - Appointment of Olivia Hart-Paulson to 
Commission on Disability.
In City Council, M. Gitschier pulled item.  No objections.
6. VOTES FROM THE CITY MANAGER
6.1. Vote - Authorize CM Ex. Release of Land Restrictions - Lowell 
Housing Authority.

In City Council, Given 2nd reading.  Motion “To Adopt” by C. Chau, 
seconded by C. Mercier.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 10 yeas (C. Chau, C. 
Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, 
C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. Scott).  So voted.  C. Robinson noted the 
restriction regarding open space.  William Martin (Attorney for Trinity 
Financial) noted open space would remain and the other restrictions should
have been released way before and this is to just to begin construction on 
housing units.  Chair was relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 6:42 PM.  M. 
Gitschier questioned ownership once the restrictions were lifted.  Chair 
returned at 6:45 PM.  C. McDonough noted his concern with Decatur 
Street.  Atty. Martin noted that there were no changes to the original intent 
of the agreement.  
7. REPORTS (SUB/COMMITTEE, IF ANY)
7.1. Rules & Election Law SC October 6, 2026.
In City Council, C. Juran provided report outlining the attendance and the 
discussion regarding update of City Council Rules and that the Law 
Department will draft them and bring before full Council for discussion.  
Motion to accept the report as a report of progress by C. Descoteaux, 
seconded by C. Chau.  So voted.  
7.2. Housing SC October 13, 2026.
In City Council, C. Robinson provided report outlining the attendance and 
the discussion regarding ordinance concerning housing standards in terms 
of tenant rights.  C. Robinson noted it was the beginning of the process and
that there will be public input on this matter.  Motion to accept the report as 
a report of progress by C. McDonough, seconded by C. Juran.  So voted.  
8. PETITIONS
8.1. Claim - (1) Property Damage.
In City Council, Motion to refer to Law Department for report and 
recommendation by C. Scott, seconded by C. Mercier.  So voted.

9. ANNOUNCEMENTS
In City Council, C. Mercier noted upcoming Bridge Club award.  C. 
Descoteaux lauded the Chelmsford Street work that was done.  M. 
Gitschier noted upcoming Bay State Marathon and the effect on City traffic.
10. ADJOURNMENT
In City Council, Motion to Adjourn by C. Descoteaux, seconded by C. 
Juran.  So voted.
Meeting adjourned at 8:03 PM.

Michael Q. Geary, City Clerk
